# beowulf-fitt-39 — reviewer, pass 1

Order followed: (1) notes against forms and positions, (2) Old English to `l`, (3) `l` and `i`, (4) remembered English in `i`, (5) published parts (grep of root `beowulf-*.json`). `units.json` edited by script only; `t` and `ln` of all 28 units verified unchanged against a copy taken before editing; the file still loads.

## Changes (line · field · severity · what was wrong · what was done)

1. 2826 · n · low · the note called ‘him’ a dative “from him” while `l` and `i` both say “took him off”, a contradiction · note now says `l`/`i` render the dative of the one affected as “took him off”, and that ‘hine’ is the accusative the verb normally takes.
2. 2826 · i · low · “whatever the hammers left of the smith’s work” added “smith’s work”, which the Old English lacks, and departed from the house “what the hammers left” · now “what the hammers left”.
3. 2832 · i · medium · “No more would he sweep …” turns ‘Nalles … hwearf’ (past, “he did not at all …”) into a future-in-the-past (“would no more”), and adds “to men” · now “He did not go sweeping through the air at midnight … nor show himself; he fell … brought down by the battle-leader’s handiwork” (house ‘handiwork’).
4. 2832 · n · low · ‘eorðan’ called a dative, but the weak feminine ending is dative and accusative alike; the note also said “that battle-leader’s” where `l` has “the” · note now says “to earth” with the ambiguity stated, and “the battle-leader’s”.
5. 2842 · n · medium · the note said ‘dryht-’ means “troop” and then that “noble” is a guess from “the second half”, which is illogical, and left `l` “lord-treasures” unexplained · rewritten: `l` is the literal sense (the lord’s company), `i` “noble” rests on ‘dryhtlīc’ and similar compounds (glossary entry ‘dryhtlīc — lordly, noble’); both guesses; “occurs only here in the poem” (checked in the Klaeber source: one occurrence).
6. 2844 · l · low · “brought the end … to its finish” says the end twice; the Old English has ‘ende gefēred’ with ‘lǣnan līfes’ depending on it · now “had accomplished the end of lent life”.
7. 2845 · l · low · “the ten troth-breakers together, the timid” scrambled ‘tȳdre trēowlogan tȳne ætsomne’ · now “the timid troth-breakers, ten together”.
8. 2845 · i · low · ‘dareðum’ is darts, not “spears” · “darts”.
9. 2850 · n · low · claimed ‘þǣr’ “is ‘to where’”; it is ‘where’ · reworded: ‘where’, and `i` supplies the coming-up.
10. 2854 · l · medium · “to him nothing did it succeed” made ‘wiht’ a noun object, but the note (rightly) takes ‘wiht ne’ as the strong negative · now “to him it did not at all succeed”.
11. 2854 · n · low · “Thorkelin read ‘spēow’” (the apparatus has him emending) and “the likely cause” of the p/wynn slip was asserted · “printed”, “a possible cause”.
12. 2858 · i · medium · `l` “as he still does” but `i` “as it still does”: the subject was changed · `i` now “as he still does”.
13. 2858 · n · low · “for each of men” in the note against “over each of men” in `l` · note now “over”.
14. 2858 · n · low · said nothing about the antecedent of ‘hē’ in ‘dêð’ (God or ‘dōm’, both masculine) · added in one clause.
15. 2860 · n · medium · “‘forlēosan’ taking a genitive (‘elne’)”: ‘elne’ is dative (the genitive of ‘ellen’ is ‘elnes’, as at 2876); ‘his’ is the possessive · corrected.
16. 2860 · i · low · “thrown away his courage” stronger than ‘forlēas’ · “lost his courage”.
17. 2864 · n · medium · said the first ‘Þæt’ looks forward to “the clause two lines on, ‘þæt hē … forwurpe’”; the clause begins at 2865 (‘þæt se mondryhten’) and ‘forwurpe’ is seven lines on, resumed by the second ‘þæt’ at 2871 · corrected; note at 2871 now says it takes up the clause begun at 2865.
18. 2865 · i · low · ‘mondryhten’ rendered “lord”; house rendering is “liege-lord” (and 2848 `i` uses it) · “liege-lord”.

20. 2871 · n · low · see 17 (resumption of the clause begun at 2865) · edited.
21. 2877 · n · low · “Klaeber’s note says ‘gifan’ is perhaps the better reading”: the apparatus says only “Perh. gifan” · reworded.
22. 2882 · i · low · “when the hard hour came upon him” is a ready-made English phrase for ‘sīo þrāg’ · rebuilt: “when the time of trial overtook him”.
23. 2884 · n · low · `i` “all that is dear” departs from `l` “love” without saying so · note now says so.

## Considered and refused

- 2821 · `i` “lying in a sorry state” for ‘blēate gebǣran’ (“bear himself wretchedly”): the note states that the sense is “lying in misery”; refused.
- 2821 · `l`/`i` “young and untried” against `l` “unwise”: the note says ‘unfrōd’ is “inexperienced, young”, and the contrast with ‘frōd’ is explained; refused.
- 2826 · `l` “might not be ruler” for ‘wealdan ne mōste’: acceptable; ‘wealdan’ governs the dative ‘bēahhordum’; refused.
- 2836 · `l` “in this”: the first ‘þæt’ is rendered as an anticipating pronoun, flagged in crux-notes and in the note as a guess; refused, though a plain “that” would be as defensible.
- 2836 · `i` “have prospered” (perfect) for ‘ðāh’ (preterite): the whole sentence is a general statement “as I have heard”; refused.
- 2836 · ‘attorsceaðan oreðe’: the note does not label the case; whether ‘attorsceaðan’ is genitive or governed by ‘wið’ is unclear; left as is.
- 2845 · “who earlier had not dared” (pluperfect for preterite ‘dorston’): normal English for ‘ǣr’; refused.
- 2852 · ‘frēan’ called a genitive: the weak ending is also dative; the genitive reading matches `l` “the lord’s shoulders”; refused.
- 2855 · `i` “anything that the Wielder willed” builds in the sense of Thorpe’s ‘willan’; but the note says that reading “gives the same sense in plainer words”, and a literal “anything of the Wielder’s” is not English; refused, left to the next pass.
- 2851/2871/2866 · `i` “war-gear” for both ‘ēoredgeatwe’ and ‘gūðgewǣdu’: set by crux-notes; `l` distinguishes them; refused.
- 2871 · `i` “in vain” for ‘wrāðe’ against `l` “bitterly”: flagged in crux-notes and the note; refused.
- 2880 · `i` “from his head” for ‘of gewitte’: declared a guess in the note; refused.
- 2862 · ‘maðelode’ rendering: matches fitts 34 and 36 (“spoke in speech-words” / “spoke in formal words”).
- Consistency with published parts: ‘Wielder’ (fitts 24, 25, 32, 33, 37), ‘That, lo, … he who’ (fitt 24, 1700), ‘liege-lord’ (fitt 36), ‘Wīglāf’ and the water (fitts 37, 38), ‘kinsman’ (fitts 36, 37) all agree; the father’s name, printed ‘Wēoxstān’ in fitt 36 and ‘Wēohstān’ here, follows Klaeber’s printing in each place.
- Italic letters and apparatus: all six italic words and every apparatus item in the packet are covered in the notes.

# Pass 2

Fresh second pass over all 28 units (notes against forms and positions; Old English to `l`; `l` and `i`; remembered English; published parts) and over every entry of `gloss.json` (all 90 novel entries and all 19 `__broaden__` entries) against the lines where each form stands. `units.json` and `gloss.json` edited by script only; `t` and `ln` of all units verified unchanged; both files load; every novel form is present in `gloss.json`; every broadened entry is the known entry whole + ` · ` + the new reading (checked against `known-forms.json`); no entry carries a line number or "here". `crux-notes.md` corrected.

## Text changes (line · form · field · severity · what was wrong · done)

1. 2828 · ac him īrenna ecga · i · medium · "for the iron edges had taken him off" turned the contrast of ‘ac’ (after ‘ne mōste’, "but") into a cause, and disagreed with `l` "but" · now "but the iron edges had taken him off".
2. 2852 · wehte · l · medium · "he shook him with water": ‘wehte’ is the past of ‘weccan’ (rouse), as the gloss already had it, not of ‘wecgan’ (shake; past ‘wegde’), and `i` already says "rouse" · now "he roused him with water".
3. 2852 · wehte · n · medium · the note derived ‘wehte’ from ‘wecgan’, "shake, move", contradicting the glossary and the form · now ‘weccan’ (‘rouse, wake’), with the ‘wegde’ remark.
4. 2855 · wiht … Wealdendes · n · low · `i` "anything that the Wielder willed" borrows the sense of Thorpe's ‘willan’ without saying so · note now says `i` supplies "willed" because "anything of the Wielder's" is not English. (Pass 1 left this to this pass.)
5. 2860 · ēðbegēte · i · medium · "The young man now had a grim answer, easily got, for anyone …" reversed the direction (‘æt ðām geongan’ = from the young man; the coward gets the answer) · now "Then it was easy for one who had earlier lost his courage to get a grim answer from the young man."
6. 2867 · þrȳð- · n · low · the note said Thorkelin read the manuscript's ‘pryd-’ as ‘þryð-’; the apparatus says Thorkelin and the editors (except Arnold, Chambers) read ‘þrȳð-’ · corrected.
7. 2871 · gūðgewǣdu · i · low · "that war-gear" adds a demonstrative the Old English lacks · "the war-gear".
8. 2874 · him God ūðe, sigora Waldend · l · low · "granted him, the Wielder of victories" reads as though "him" were the Wielder · now "yet to him God, the Wielder of victories, granted that …".
9. 2877 · Wīglāf a kinsman · n · low · ‘Wægmunding’ is spelled ‘Wǣgmunding’ in the source (2607, 2814) · respelled.
10. 2884 · sincþego · n · low · the note glossed the second element as ‘þigu’, the glossary (and the form) have ‘þegu’ · aligned.

## Gloss changes (form · severity · what was wrong · done)

1. forgolden · medium · "the thing paid for is in the dative, the price too": in the line the share (‘dǣl’) is the nominative subject and only ‘dēaðe’ (the price) is a dative · now "the price is in the dative".
2. sǣmra · medium · parsed "neuter"; the comparative ending ‘-a’ is the weak masculine nominative (neuter would be ‘-e’), and the dragon is the subject · now "nominative singular masculine, declined weak as comparatives are".
3. lufen · medium · "love, joy" and "some take it as ‘hope’" are not supported by the packet's apparatus (alternatives are ‘leofen’ "sustenance", ‘lēofum’, ‘lungre’) · rewritten on the apparatus; "joy" and "hope" dropped.
4. drep · low · "here with e" (pinned) · "this form has e".
5. homera · low · "here as the maker" (pinned) · "as the maker".
6. helpan (broadened) · low · "here with the genitive" (pinned) · "with the genitive"; the old entry is still whole.
7. gehwæs (broadened) · low · "genitive singular neuter, agreeing with dǣda": a singular cannot agree with the plural ‘dǣda’ · now the masculine/neuter genitive form standing with the feminine plural; old entry whole.
8. elne (broadened) · low · asserted that ‘forlēosan’ "takes the dative", which nothing here establishes · now "dative with forlēas"; old entry whole.
9. fornāmon · low · "takes a dative of the one robbed" ignores the accusative ‘hine’ that other editors print · "dative (or accusative)".

## Considered and refused

- All pass-1 refusals stand (2821 "sorry state" and "young and untried"; 2826 "might not be ruler"; 2836 "in this" and "have prospered"; 2845 pluperfect; 2852 ‘frēan’ genitive; 2851/2871/2866 "war-gear" twice; 2871 "in vain"; 2880 "from his head").
- 2871, 2873 · `l` "his war-garments", "his war-companions": possessive supplied where the Old English has none, but it is the natural English and does not change the sense; refused.
- 2821 · note calls ‘wæs gegongen’ an "impersonal passive"; it is an impersonal perfect with the participle, but the label serves the reader and nothing in `l`/`i` depends on it; refused.
- 2886 · note "‘Mōt’ is ‘may, must’ … as in ‘may go about empty’": clumsy but true; refused.
- Gloss · mǣgburge "dependent on londrihtes or ǣghwylc": both readings are possible from the word order; the hedge is honest; refused.
- Gloss · sǣmra "the positive is not found", dryhtmāðma "noble treasure", unfrōdum number remark: not contradicted by anything in the packet; refused.
- Gloss · ecga "nominative plural with the ending -a" and ecge "accusative … after wið": the second is part of the old entry (not mine to rewrite); the first is the only reading that gives ‘fornāmon’ a plural subject; refused.
- Gloss · fēðecempa, wīlāf (lemma spelled with þ / with g): variant spellings are stated in the entries; refused.
- Italic letters, apparatus items and consistency with published parts (fitts 34, 36, 37, 38; ‘Wielder’, ‘liege-lord’, ‘maðelode’, ‘hall-sitters’, ‘handiwork’) rechecked: no further change.
- Father's name: ‘Wīhstān’ (2752), ‘Wēohstān’ (2613, 2862), ‘Wēoxstān’ (2602) are Klaeber's printings; the note follows the line it stands in.
